cases.name: unknown-gen-attribute
cases.description: An attribute no generator reads

cases.name: weight-on-inline-values
cases.description: weight= on inline values — percent= is for that

cases.name: weight-without-column
cases.description: weight= needs a column to weight

cases.name: weight-with-order
cases.description: weight= and order= contradict each other
cases.config: <tdc><env count="2" seed="s"><sequence name="G"><gen type="file" src="x.csv" column="c" weight="w" order="sequential"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>x</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: http-without-src
cases.description: A service generator with no endpoint

cases.name: http-src-not-a-url
cases.description: An endpoint that is not an http URL

cases.name: http-in-names-nothing
cases.description: in= pointing at a sequence nobody declared

cases.name: http-bad-timeout
cases.description: timeout= that is not a positive number of SECONDS. Left unchecked the five disagreed twice over: four fell back to the default in silence, Python threw at run time, and Python read the attribute as milliseconds

cases.name: http-bad-on-error
cases.description: on_error outside the two allowed values

cases.name: unsupported-binary-operator
cases.description: An operator the evaluator does not implement

cases.name: unsupported-unary-operator
cases.description: A unary operator the evaluator does not implement

cases.name: invalid-mask
cases.description: A mask that does not parse

cases.name: malformed-repeat
cases.description: A repeat that is not a count or a range

cases.name: repeat-on-a-mix
cases.description: repeat on a mix, which picks one branch rather than a list

cases.name: flag-on-a-nested-mix
cases.description: A nested mix cannot own a flag column

cases.name: anomaly-without-a-flag
cases.description: A branch marked as the outlier with nothing recording it

cases.name: unknown-child-of-case
cases.description: A tag a case body has no meaning for
cases.config: <tdc><env count="2" seed="s"><mix name="M" percent="100"><case><sequence name="Q"><gen type="text" value="a"/></sequence></case></mix></env><block><line><data>x</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: computed-member-access
cases.description: Subscripting in an if expression, which the evaluator does not implement

cases.name: repeat-on-a-counter
cases.description: A counter's value follows the row index, and a list of unknown length leaves no index to follow. The message names the type.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="X"><gen type="increment" value="1" repeat="3"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{X}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: gen-count-is-not-a-gen-attribute
cases.description: count= is the run on <env> and the table on <pool>; a <gen> reads neither, and the value looks like a way to ask for several values
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="A"><gen type="text" value="a,b" count="99"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{A}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: gen-flag-belongs-to-mix
cases.description: flag= records which branch a <mix> took; the <gen> equivalent is anomaly_flag=
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="A"><gen type="text" value="a,b" flag="X"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{A}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: cycle-without-a-walk
cases.description: cycle= says what happens when a walk runs out — without order="sequential" the generator draws, and a draw never runs out
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="A"><gen type="text" value="a,b" cycle="false"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{A}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: order-on-a-template-generator
cases.description: A pack's parameters are open-ended, but which type reads order= does not depend on the pack
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="A"><gen type="template" value="person.lastName" order="sequential"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{A}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: parent-on-a-template-generator
cases.description: parent= filters a whole <sequence>; on a <gen> it was accepted and read by nobody
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="A"><gen type="template" value="person.lastName" parent="X.y"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{A}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: local-on-a-generator-is-real
cases.description: local= on a <gen> DOES override the locale for that generator — the sweep called it a no-op and measuring said otherwise
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="A"><gen type="template" value="person.lastName" local="ru"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{A}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: interpolation-in-an-attribute-that-does-not-expand-it
cases.description: Interpolation reaches the text inside <data> and <gen type="template" value=>, and nowhere else. Written anywhere else the braces are literal characters, and the generator that receives them used to complain about whatever it happened to be parsing: an invalid number range here, an invalid date on a date, a bad quantifier on a regex, an unknown alphabet on a symbol — and type="text" said nothing at all and emitted the braces. One cause, six answers, none of them naming it. TDC263 names it, and REPLACES the generator's own complaint rather than sitting beside it.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="1" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="N"><gen type="text" value="5"/></sequence><sequence name="X"><gen type="number" value="1..${{N}}"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{X}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: interpolation-in-a-date-bound
cases.description: The same mistake one generator across: from= reads a date, not a column. The reader has seen ${{}} work in a template value and moved it, which is the most natural thing in the world.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="1" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="N"><gen type="text" value="5"/></sequence><sequence name="X"><gen type="date" from="${{N}}" to="2026-12-31"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{X}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: date-vocabulary-on-a-number
cases.description: from=/to= are the natural words for a numeric range and a number generator has never read them: <gen type="number" from="1000" to="9999"/> produced single digits and check called it valid.

cases.name: date-format-on-a-number
cases.description: format= and precision= belong to the date generator; on a number they are accepted and read by nothing.

cases.name: the-birth-window-on-a-text
cases.description: oldest=/youngest= bound the year a birthday is drawn from. Nothing else reads them.

cases.name: number-shape-on-a-text
cases.description: length= sizes a drawn number or symbol string. A text walks the list you gave it, so the attribute reached nothing.

cases.name: number-shape-on-a-regex
cases.description: A regex is as long as its pattern says; length= there is read by nothing.

cases.name: decimals-on-a-text
cases.description: decimals= rounds a number. Four generators produce one; a text produces characters, which have no places.

cases.name: regex-ceiling-on-a-text
cases.description: regex_max_length= caps what an unbounded pattern may expand to, and only the two regex generators expand patterns.

cases.name: percent-is-deliberately-not-owned
cases.description: The line the ownership table must not cross. Only text and number read percent= as a share of their own values, yet the engine routes ANY generator carrying it through the share machinery, and both shapes below validate today. Owning the name would refuse them.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="4" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="G"><gen type="regex" value="[a-z]{3}" percent="70"/><gen type="regex" value="[0-9]{3}"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{G}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: row-link-with-mixed-order
cases.description: row= keeps a record together by making every member read the SAME line of the file. order="sequential" on some members and not others breaks that: one picks by position while the other draws at random, so John was paired with Johnson when John's last name is Smith — and check called it valid. The two TDC061s are the missing users.csv, not part of what this pins.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="6" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="U"><gen name="F" type="file" src="users.csv" column="first_name" row="u" order="sequential"/><gen name="L" type="file" src="users.csv" column="last_name" row="u"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{U.F}} ${{U.L}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: row-link-sequential-throughout
cases.description: The other side of the same boundary: every member of the link walks in step, so both rules pick by position and the records hold. Only the missing file is reported.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="6" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="U"><gen name="F" type="file" src="users.csv" column="first_name" row="u" order="sequential"/><gen name="L" type="file" src="users.csv" column="last_name" row="u" order="sequential"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{U.F}} ${{U.L}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: row-link-across-two-files
cases.description: One row= key over two different files — the members live in different sequences, which is where a per-sequence check cannot see them
cases.config: <tdc><env count="4" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="N"><gen type="file" src="a.csv" column="name" row="k"/></sequence><sequence name="P"><gen type="file" src="b.csv" column="price" row="k"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{N}},${{P}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-date-offset-refuses-a-wrapper-it-never-reads
cases.description: A date measured from another column is the fourth member of the derived family — running, stat and formula are the other three — and it was the one nobody added. mask=, case=, missing=, missing_as=, anomaly=, repeat= and percent= all sat on it doing nothing while `check` called the config valid; measured over six rows, each byte-identical to the plain run. `missing="0.9"` blanking 0 of 6 rows is the sharpest: a reader asking for gaps got a full column. Keyed on of= rather than on the type, because a plain type="date" reads every one of them correctly.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="6" seed="a"><sequence name="D"><gen type="date" value="2024-01-01..2024-12-31"/></sequence><sequence name="L"><gen type="date" of="D" plus="7d" missing="0.9"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{L}}</data></line></block></tdc>
